s: Attorney General of India:
o: Is not entitled of audience except the Supreme Court
He gives advice to the President on legal matters
Cannot participate in the proceedings in the House of
Is a whole time counsel for the government
x: The Attorney-General for India is the highest law officer of the country and the chief legal adviser to the Government of India. He advises the Government of India, upon such legal matters as referred to him by the President. Under Article 76(3), the Attorney-General has the right of audience in all courts within the territory of India for the performance of his duties. Under Article 88 of the Constitution, every Minister and the Attorney-General of India has the right to speak in, and otherwise take part in, the proceedings of either House, in any joint sitting of the Houses, and in any parliamentary committee of which he may be named a member; however, he is not entitled to vote. The Attorney-General is not treated as a full-time government servant. With permission, he may also engage in private legal practice.

s: Who among the following is the legal adviser of a State Government?
x: The Advocate General is the official legal adviser to the State Government (Art. 165(2)); the AG and SG serve the Union.

s: Who advises the State Government on legal matters?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: It shall be the duty of the Advocate-General to advise the Government of the State on legal matters [Article 165(2)]. The Governor of each State shall appoint a person, who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court, as the Advocate- General for the State [Article 165(1)]. The Advocate-General shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor [Article 165 (3)]. He is the first legal advisor to the State Government.

s: Solicitor General of India is ……..?
x: The Solicitor General of India is subordinate to the Attorney General of India. The Solicitor- General of India is the second law officer of the country, assists the Attorney- General, and is himself assisted by several Additional Solicitor-Generals of India.

s: Who appoints Advocate General of State in India?
x: Under Art. 165(1) the Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor, not the Chief Minister or the Law Minister.

s: In India, who is known as the highest law officer?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
x: The Attorney General is the highest law officer of India; the Advocate General is only the State's highest law officer.

s: Which Articles provide the legislative privileges of the Attorney General and of the Advocate General, respectively?
x: Article 105(4) extends parliamentary privileges to the Attorney General and Article 194(4) extends State legislative privileges to the Advocate General. Articles 88 and 177 give the right to speak, and Articles 76 and 165 create the offices.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Advocate General of a State?
x: The Advocate General is provided for under Article 165 (Part VI); the Attorney General under Article 76 (Part V).

s: Who appoints the Solicitor General of India?
x: The Solicitor General is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, while the President appoints the Attorney General.

s: Which law officer has the right to speak in Parliament under Article 88?
x: Article 88 rights belong to the Attorney General; the Solicitor General has no floor rights in Parliament.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Solicitor General — Second law officer of India
Chief Justice of India — Government's first law officer
Attorney General — Constitutional office under Article 76
Attorney General — Chief legal adviser to the Government of India
x: The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary, not the government's first law officer. The Attorney General is the chief legal adviser and first law officer of India.

s: In which Part of the Constitution is the office of the Attorney General of India (Article 76) provided?
x: Article 76 (Attorney General) is in Part V; the Advocate General (Art. 165) is in Part VI.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution of India, has the National Commission for Scheduled Castes been constituted?
x: Article 338 of the Constitution, originally provided for the establishment of a Special Officer for Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes (SCs and STs) to look into any issues pertaining to constitutional safeguards for the SCs and STs and to report to the President on their workings. Later, the 65th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1990, provided for the establishment of a high-level multi-member National Commission for SCs and STs in the place of a single Special Officer for SCs and STs. Again, the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003, bifurcated the combined National Commission for SCs and STs into two separate bodies, namely, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (under Article 338) and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (under Article 338-A).

s: The Provision of National Commission for Scheduled Tribes is given in which Article of the Constitution?
x: The provision of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes has been made by Article 338-A. Originally, there was only Article 338 for the establishment of a commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (both), but the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the combined commission into two separate bodies. Article 338A was inserted for a separate commission for Scheduled Tribes. Article 338 now only provides for a commission for Scheduled Castes. The commissions constituted under Article 338 and 338A consist of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and three other members.

s: Article 338 of the Indian Constitution deals with
x: Article 338 now provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes; 338A is for STs and 338B for backward classes.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment bifurcated the Combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into two separate bodies?
x: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes was bifurcated into the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and the National Commission for Scheduled tribes through the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003. The two commissions have been constituted under Article 338 and Article 338A, respectively.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution the Separate Scheduled Tribe Commission was established?
x: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was established by amending Article 338 and inserting a new Article 338A in the Constitution through the Constitution (89th Amendment) Act, 2003.

s: Article 338 of the Indian Constitution mandates formation of which of the following Commissions?
x: Article 338 provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes. NCW, NCM and NHRC are statutory bodies, not created by Article 338.

s: Under which Article is the National Commission for Backward Classes provided for?
x: The NCSC, NCST and NCBC fall under Articles 338, 338A and 338B respectively.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment created the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

Consider the following statements with reference to Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities :
1. In the Constitution, there is a provision for the post of Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities for every State.
2. A new Article 350 B was added for this by the 9th Constitution Amendment Act.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: The Section 21 of the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956 added new Articles-350A and 350B which provide for ‘Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage’ and ‘Special Officer for linguistic minorities’, respectively. According to clause (1) of Article 350B, there shall be a special officer for linguistic minorities to be appointed by the President. It provides for special officer for linguistic minorities at the Union level (for All India) and not for each State. This Officer in India is named Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities in India. Hence, both statements in the question are not correct.
